description: Order a handful of errands against a hard arrival time, and say honestly whether they fit. This is the "pick up a prescription, get petrol, and be at the school by quarter past three" tool. Give `origin`, `destination` (+ `destination_name`), `arrive_by` (RFC 3339 with an offset: convert "quarter past three" yourself), optional `depart_at`, and 1 to 5 `errands`. Each errand is EITHER a `category` (a kind of place: "pharmacy", "fuel", "supermarket", or a colloquial phrase the server normalises; use `list_place_categories` for the vocabulary) OR a `place` {lat, lon} the driver already knows ("the school", "the nursery"). Resolve a named place with `geocode` first and pass the coordinate: never invent one. Optional `dwell_minutes` per errand (default 5). The server chooses the order and the actual shops, exhaustively, over engine-computed travel times -- do NOT attempt the ordering or the arithmetic yourself. IMPORTANT: `feasible: false` is an ANSWER, not an error to retry. It names the errand that costs the most (`blocking_errand`), says how late the whole chain would be (`over_by_s`), and returns the stops of the chain that DOES fit with `dropped` naming what had to go. Tell the driver what to drop. Every stop is a real indexed place carrying its id: never mention a shop the answer did not return. `hours` is "open_on_the_tag" (the map's tag covers your arrival, which is evidence and not a promise) or "unknown" (most places carry no hours at all); a place the tag proves shut is never proposed. ALWAYS show `usage_note`: this is planned before setting off or by a passenger, never at the wheel. Requires the MapMap gateway.

ErrandSpec.description:
One errand in a `plan_errands` chain: a kind of place to find, or a
place the caller already knows.

category.description:
The KIND of place wanted: a category from `list_place_categories`
("pharmacy", "fuel", "supermarket"), or a colloquial phrase the
server normalises ("petrol station", "chemist"). Use this for
anything the driver described by what it is rather than by name.

dwell_minutes.description: How long the driver is out of the car here, minutes (default 5).

id.description:
What to call this errand in the answer ("prescription", "petrol").
Defaults to the category, or to "stop N".

place.description:
A specific place the driver already knows, as a coordinate. Use
this for "the school", "the nursery", "Mum's": places the map
cannot be expected to resolve from the words alone. Resolve a NAMED
place with `geocode` first and pass the coordinate here; never
guess one.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

arrive_by.description:
The hard arrival time, RFC 3339 with an offset
("2026-09-21T15:15:00+01:00"). Convert "quarter past three" to an
absolute instant in the driver's own offset before calling.

depart_at.description: When they set off, RFC 3339. Defaults to now.

destination.description: Where they have to be by `arrive_by`.

destination_name.description: What to call the destination in the answer ("the school").

errands.description:
The errands, in any order: the answer decides the order. One to
five.

max_detour_minutes.description:
How far off the direct route a candidate place may sit, as a detour
in minutes (default 12, at most 45).

origin.description: Where the driver sets off from.

name: plan_errands

ErrandStop.description: One planned stop in an errand chain.

drive_s.description: Driving time of the leg into this stop, seconds.

hours.description:
What the map's opening-hours tag says about the arrival time:
"open_on_the_tag" (the tag covers it, which is evidence and NOT a
promise) or "unknown" (no usable tag). A stop the tag proves shut
is never proposed, so "closed" never appears here.

hours_tag.description: The tag itself, when the map carries one.

id.description:
The index id, for an indexed place. Its presence is what makes the
stop checkable; a stop without one is a coordinate the caller gave.

kind.description:
"category" for a place the index found, "place" for one the caller
supplied.

label.description: Its full label, for reading aloud.

arrival.description:
When the plan arrives, RFC 3339. Present whenever there is a plan,
including the reduced plan on an infeasible answer.

attribution.description: Credit owed for the place data, when the answer used the index.

blocking_errand.description: The errand that costs the most time, when the deadline is missed.

corridor_note.description:
**Always present.** What the corridor search did and did not look
at. An empty answer is a statement about this index and this
corridor, never about what exists on the ground.

departure.description: When the driver sets off, RFC 3339.

dropped.description:
Errands that had to be dropped for the plan to fit. Empty when
feasible.

failed_errand.description:
The errand a "no_candidates_in_corridor" or "all_candidates_closed"
answer is about.

feasible.description:
**Whether every errand fits before the deadline.** False is an
ANSWER, not an error: report `reason`, the errand named in
`blocking_errand`, and what `dropped` says has to go.

geometry_polyline6.description: The planned journey as an encoded polyline6.

opening_hours_note.description:
**Always present.** How opening hours were used, and how little of
the map carries them.

over_by_s.description: How late the whole chain would be, seconds.

reason.description: The same cause in plain language, for the driver.

reason_code.description:
Machine token for why the chain does not fit: "deadline_missed",
"destination_unreachable_in_time", "no_candidates_in_corridor",
"all_candidates_closed" or "unroutable".

stops.description:
The stops, in visit order. On an infeasible answer these are the
stops of the reduced plan, the one that DOES fit.

total_dwell_s.description: Total time out of the car, seconds.

usage_note.description:
**Always present.** Why this is planned stationary rather than at
the wheel. Show it.

verification_note.description:
**Always present.** That every stop is an indexed place or a
supplied coordinate, never a generated one.
